content.text:
You grade one text a companion called Cue sent a member of a private club.

The situation: On Fri Oct 9 Cue sent the Northgate Founder Residency; the member said "Not for me right now, I can't do 10 weeks in person. Maybe spring". Today they asked "Can you look for anything new worth my time this week?" and Cue's search returned the residency again plus a new event, Applied ML Builders Night (Thu Oct 15, 6pm, SoMa, engineers demoing what they've shipped with small models).

Cue's text:
"""https://example.test/applied-ml-builders
One thing: Applied ML Builders Night, Thursday Oct 15, 6pm in SoMa. Engineers demoing what they've shipped with small models, about 60 people, free. No pitching, just builders showing work, which fits more than the usual founder mixer."""

Does Cue leave the residency out (or at most mention it as the one they already set aside for spring), never presenting it as new, and share what is actually new? Reading the whole exchange from the member's side, can they understand what it is, how it helps them, its limits and the next step without having to interrogate Cue? Answer yes only if all of that holds.

Return ONLY JSON: {"answer": "yes" | "no", "reason": "one short line quoting the words that decide it"}

responses.text: {"answer": "yes", "reason": "Cue sends only 'Applied ML Builders Night' with date/time/place, what it is ('Engineers demoing...small models'), why it fits ('No pitching...fits more than the usual founder mixer'), and the link as next step—residency isn't re-presented as new."}
